notes: Supplied locators do not identify a particular outcome or contrast. All five assigned original descriptions and p.4 locators are identical; no assignment by audit ID/order is justified. On p.4 section 3.5, omnibus Wald chi-square candidates are ARFID/NIAS 67.52, traditional eating disorder symptoms/EAT-26 26.07, and psychological distress/K10 39.22, each p < .01; BMI is 2.07, p = .56. Pairwise candidates printed in the same section: ARFID emotional over-and-under versus non-emotional 53.19, versus over-eating 54.10, versus under-eating 32.76, and under-eating versus over-eating 7.75 (all p < .01); non-emotional versus over-eating 2.35, p = .13. Traditional symptoms: mixed versus non-emotional 19.90, p < .01; mixed versus under-eating 10.95, p < .01; mixed versus over-eating 2.18, p = .14. Psychological distress: mixed versus non-emotional 35.50, versus over-eating 12.10, versus under-eating 31.31 (all p < .01); other three pattern contrasts all p > .05. These are printed candidate statistics, not assigned target values. Section 3.4 also gives demographic-predictor ORs; Table 2 gives LCA model fit/p-values. Sample 1,068 is explicitly described as the study sample (p.2 and Table 1 p.3), not an explicit target-specific complete-case analytic N. Missingness ranges 0–4.9%; incomplete data were not imputed (p.3 section 2.3). No target-test analytic N or explicit final-group counts establish an allowable sum. No N derived from percentages or df. Rendered and visually inspected supplied PDF p.4 at /home/lukas/.cache/fred-completion-renders/8be011c5dd0245e7/page4.png; canonical text remains evidence source.
